title: Rest pose must reproduce the generated mesh (PoseRotationResolver drops bind roll)
description:
## Summary
The skinned mesh deforms with no animation. At rest the rendered mesh must be identical to the generated mesh, because bind poses are the inverse of the rest frames and Unity deforms with `Σ w_i · bones[i] · bindPose[i] · v`. `CreatureRig.ApplyPose(PosedSkeleton.FromRestPose(snapshot))` runs at generation, so the applied rig rotations come from `PoseRotationResolver.ResolveIntoCompatible`. That resolver re-derives each non-terminal bone's rotation with `Quaternion.LookRotation(posedChildDirection, restUp)`, which (a) cannot reproduce a bind rotation that carries roll and (b) is undefined for non-segment bones that have children. At rest the applied rotation therefore differs from the bind rotation and the mesh drifts.

## User Mandate
> Here is the differences between the non-animated raw mesh and the unmodified animated mesh (straight out of the generation phase). Note that it moves a bit, especially the legs. I would think an unmodified animated model should stay exactly still. This is also the amount of squish that happens when the back moves, for reference.

STRICT. An unmodified (rest) animated model must match the generated mesh exactly.

## Evidence (EditMode probe `PoseRotationRestIdentityProbeTests`)
`PoseRotationResolver.ResolveIntoCompatible(rest, FromRestPose(rest))` must reproduce `rest[i].Rotation` for every bone.
- Rest round trip for a canonical segment chain (`Rotation = LookRotation(segmentDir, up)`): PASSES.
- `RestRoundTrip_SegmentBoneWithRolledRotation`: FAILS — `seg0` bind `Quaternion.Euler(0,30,0)` comes back 120° off.
- `RestRoundTrip_NonSegmentBoneWithChild`: FAILS — `part_root` identity bind comes back 120° off.
Mechanism: `LookRotation` forces the baked forward onto the direction-to-child and re-derives roll, discarding the authored bind rotation.

## Scope
- Change `PoseRotationResolver.ResolveIntoCompatible` so a bone at its rest position keeps its exact rest rotation.
- Proposed: aim delta `FromToRotation(restDirection, posedDirection) * restRotation`, where both directions are measured between the bone and the same reference child in the REST vs POSED snapshots (segment continuation child, or primary child for non-segment bones). At rest the two directions are equal, so the delta is identity and the bind rotation is preserved; posed it still aims the bone at the child and preserves twist.
- Keep terminal bones at their rest rotation. Keep the deterministic child selection.
- No new DNA mutation path; runtime remains pure.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `PoseRotationRestIdentityProbeTests` all pass.
- Existing `PoseRotationResolverTests` / `CreatureRigTests` pose contracts still pass, or every intentional contract change is documented with evidence and surfaced to the user.
- The rendered rest skinned mesh matches the generated mesh (PlayMode / manual check).

## Related
- TSK-0194 clusters C/D (LBS parity + `body_j2` fixture drift) — the same rest/bind mismatch shows up as SMR-vs-LBS-oracle vertex deltas.
- TSK-0113 (PoseRotationResolver determinism), TSK-0119 (owns the pose contract tests per TSK-0194).
- TSK-0215 (rig bone rotation snap) — sibling editor fix; not the cause of this drift.

comments.body:
## Rest-pose identity fixed (2026-09-11)

### Root cause
`PoseRotationResolver.ResolveIntoCompatible` rebuilt every non-terminal bone rotation with `Quaternion.LookRotation(posedChildDirection, restUp)`:
- A bind rotation carrying roll cannot be reproduced by `LookRotation` (roll is re-derived).
- Non-segment bones that have children (part attachment bones such as eyes with pupils) have no segment direction at all.

`CreatureRig.ApplyPose(PosedSkeleton.FromRestPose(snapshot))` runs at generation, so those re-derived rotations were applied to the rig while the bind poses still described the authored rest frames. `bones[i] != rest_i` breaks the skinning identity, so the rendered mesh deformed with no animation.

### Fix
Swing-from-rest aim delta:
`rotations[i] = Quaternion.FromToRotation(restDirection, posedDirection) * bone.Rotation`,
where both directions are measured between the bone and the **same** reference child (segment continuation child for segment bones, primary child otherwise) in the REST vs POSED snapshots. At rest the two directions are equal, the delta is identity, and the exact bind rotation is preserved. Posed, the bone still aims at the same child and keeps its authored roll. Degenerate/non-finite directions fall back to the bind rotation. `ResolveLookRotation` was removed (dead after the change).

### Evidence
New EditMode `PoseRotationRestIdentityProbeTests` (3): a canonical segment chain already round-tripped; `RestRoundTrip_SegmentBoneWithRolledRotation` and `RestRoundTrip_NonSegmentBoneWithChild` failed by ~120° before the fix and pass now.

Full EditMode **164/164** (148 baseline + 16 new).

### Intentional contract change (surfaced)
Two existing assertions encoded the old force-align contract and were updated with documented rationale:
- `PoseRotationResolverTests.Resolve_ChildDirectionDrivesNonTerminalRotation`: now asserts the swing on the bone's rest direction instead of on `Vector3.forward`.
- `PoseRotationResolverTests.Resolve_SegmentedChainUsesPosedContinuationChild`: `segment_1`'s geometric direction is unchanged between rest and posed, so it must keep its rest rotation.
- `CreatureRigTests.BuildAndApplyPose_...`: a translation-only pose must not rotate a bone; asserts the bind rotation is preserved.

For real inferred skeletons the bind rotation is built as `LookRotation(segmentDirection, up)`, so forward == rest direction and behaviour is unchanged; only bind-inconsistent bones (the drift case) change.

### Residual
- The 3 pre-existing PlayMode skinning failures in `CreatureSkinnedMeshRendererTests` are unchanged (identical vertex deltas). They compare the Unity SMR against an LBS oracle that consumes the same rotations, so they are a bind-pose/weights/Unity-SMR-semantics issue, not this resolver. Remain owned by TSK-0194 clusters C/D.
- A PlayMode/manual check that the rendered rest mesh now matches the generated mesh is still outstanding (MCP cannot diff rendered meshes here).

## User confirmation (2026-09-12)
> Much better, both are confirmed fixed

The rendered rest mesh now matches the generated mesh (user-confirmed in the editor), and the rest-pose identity probe plus the full EditMode suite are green. Closing as Done on user acceptance. The 3 pre-existing PlayMode skinning failures remain owned by TSK-0194 clusters C/D.
